newsitem.title: UK: De Le Rue says to revamp print operations.
newsitem.headline: De Le Rue says to revamp print operations.

text.p: Britain's De La Rue Plc said on Monday it was reorganising its security print manufacturing sites in order to remain competitive and meet future needs in its industry.
The reorganisation, which would cost around 15 million stg, will save the company around seven million stg per annum after completion, De La Rue said.
Earlier, De La Rue used to produce a range of products in each of its plants. According to new plan, the manufacturing will be consolidated on product by site basis.
The company said the plan would "control costs, maximise overall efficiency and further improve service to customers".
The Dunstable unit will be closed down and its security print operations will transfer to High Wycombe.

The reorganisation would result in around 400 redundancies across its various sites, De La Rue said. The company would offer some employees the opportunity to transfer to its High Wycome unit from its Dunstable unit.
The manufacture of travellers cheques would be transferred from its Gateshead factory to Thomas De La Rue Inc in Washington and to its recently-acquired Harrison & Sons Ltd at High Wycombe.
The company's production of banknotes would be transferred from High Wycombe to Gateshead and other worldwide banknote locations.
